title_en: Regulations on Power Grid Dispatching Management

articles.content_en: Article 1 These Regulations are formulated to strengthen the management of power grid dispatching, ensure the safety of the power grid, protect the interests of users, and meet the needs of economic construction and the people's livelihood.

Article 2 As used in these Regulations, "power grid dispatching" refers to the organization, command, guidance, and coordination of power grid operation conducted by the power grid dispatching institution (hereinafter referred to as the dispatching institution) for ensuring safe, high-quality, and economical operation of the power grid.
Power grid dispatching shall comply with the requirements of the socialist market economy and the objective laws of power grid operation.

Article 3 Power generation, power supply, and power consumption units within the territory of the People's Republic of China, as well as other relevant entities and individuals, must comply with these Regulations.
Article 4 The operation of the power grid shall adhere to the principle of unified dispatching and hierarchical management.

Article 5 No entity or individual shall distribute or use electric power and energy in excess of the plan; in the event of special circumstances requiring changes to the plan, approval must be obtained from the department that issued the electricity consumption plan.
Article 6 The administrative department of electric power under the State Council shall be in charge of power grid dispatching work.

Article 7 The functions and powers of the dispatching institution and the principles for dividing the scope of its dispatching jurisdiction shall be determined by the administrative department of electric power under the State Council.
Article 8 The principles for delimiting power plants directly dispatched by the dispatching institution shall be determined by the administrative department of electric power under the State Council.

Article 9 The dispatching system includes dispatching institutions at various levels and the operational duty units of power plants and substations within the power grid.
Dispatching institutions at lower levels must obey the dispatch of dispatching institutions at higher levels.
The operational duty units of power plants and substations within the dispatching jurisdiction of a dispatching institution must obey the dispatch of that dispatching institution.

Article 10 Dispatching institutions are divided into five levels: the national dispatching institution, dispatching institutions across provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government, dispatching institutions at the provincial, autonomous region, and municipality directly under the Central Government level, dispatching institutions at the level of cities under provincial jurisdiction, and dispatching institutions at the county level.

Dispatchers on duty shall undergo training, pass examinations, and obtain qualification certificates before they may take up their posts.
The measures for training and examination of dispatchers on duty shall be formulated by the administrative department of electric power under the State Council.

The trans-provincial power grid management departments and provincial power grid management departments shall compile power generation and supply plans, and submit such plans to the administrative department of electric power under the State Council for filing.
The dispatching institution shall compile and issue the dispatching plans for power generation and supply.
Dispatchers on duty may, in accordance with the relevant provisions and based on the operation conditions of the power grid, adjust the daily dispatching plans for power generation and supply. When adjusting the daily dispatching plans for power generation and supply, the dispatchers on duty must fill in the dispatch log.

When compiling power generation and supply plans, or when the dispatching institution compiles dispatching plans for power generation and supply, the trans-provincial power grid management departments and provincial power grid management departments shall base such plans on the plans issued by the State, the relevant power supply agreements and grid connection agreements, the equipment capacity of the power grid, and shall maintain a reserve capacity.
For reservoirs of hydropower plants (stations) with comprehensive benefits, the water storage of the reservoirs shall be reasonably utilized in accordance with the approved design documents of the hydropower plants (stations), taking into account the requirements of flood control, irrigation, power generation, environmental protection, navigation, etc.
The dispatching institution must implement the power supply plan issued by the State, and shall not withhold electric power and energy, and shall ensure the quality of power supply.

A power plant must operate in accordance with the dispatching plan and the specified voltage range issued by the dispatching institution, and shall adjust its power output and voltage according to the dispatching instructions.
The maintenance of power generation and supply equipment shall be subject to the unified arrangement of the dispatching institution.

Provincial power grid management departments, power grid management departments of cities under provincial jurisdiction, and county-level power grid management departments shall, based on the requirements of the production dispatching department of the local people's government, the characteristics of users, and the needs of safe operation of the power grid, propose a sequence table for limiting power supply in the event of accidents and over-plan power consumption. After the table is examined by the production dispatching department of the local people's government and approved by the local people's government, it shall be implemented by the dispatching institution.
The work of power limitation and overall grid dispatching shall gradually realize automated management.

Without the permission of the dispatcher on duty, no one shall operate any equipment within the dispatching jurisdiction of the dispatching institution.
Where the operation of the power grid encounters a situation endangering the safety of personnel and equipment, the personnel on duty of the unit responsible for the operation of the power plant or substation may handle it in accordance with the relevant provisions, and shall immediately report to the dispatcher of the relevant dispatching institution after handling.
Article 21 The dispatcher on duty shall issue various dispatch orders in accordance with the regulations.

Article 22 In the dispatch system, dispatch orders shall be executed. If a dispatcher on duty believes that the execution of a dispatch order would endanger personal safety or equipment safety, such dispatcher shall immediately report to the dispatcher on duty who issued the order, and the latter shall decide whether to execute or revoke the dispatch order.

Article 23 Where the person in charge of the power grid management department, the person in charge of the dispatching institution, or the person in charge of a power plant or substation has any objection to a dispatch order issued by the dispatcher on duty of the superior dispatching institution, such person may raise the objection to the administrative department of electric power of the superior power grid or the superior dispatching institution; however, before a reply is given, the dispatcher on duty of the dispatch system shall execute the dispatch order issued by the dispatcher on duty of the superior dispatching institution.

Article 24 No unit or individual shall, in violation of these Regulations, interfere with the issuance or execution of dispatch orders by the dispatcher on duty of the dispatch system; the dispatcher on duty of the dispatch system, when performing official duties according to law, shall have the right to refuse any illegal interference.
Article 25 A power plant or power grid that operates in a grid-connected manner shall be subject to the unified dispatch of the dispatching institution.

Article 26 Where a power plant and a power grid, or two power grids, need to operate in a grid-connected manner, they shall, before grid connection, conclude a grid connection agreement based on the principles of equality, mutual benefit, and consensus through consultation, and shall strictly implement such agreement.

Article 28 The dispatching institution shall give a warning to a user that consumes electricity exceeding the plan; if, after the warning, the user still fails to consume electricity according to the plan, the dispatching institution may issue an order to limit electricity consumption, and may forcibly deduct the over-consumed electricity capacity and energy; when the over-plan electricity consumption endangers the safe operation of the power grid, the dispatching institution may temporarily suspend power supply in part or in whole.

Article 29 Where, in violation of these Regulations, the planned power supply is not followed, or the power supply plan is adjusted without cause, the power grid shall, based on the user's needs, make up for the shortfall in power capacity and energy.

Article 30 Where a violation of these Regulations constitutes a public security violation, the offender shall be punished in accordance with the relevant provisions of the Public Security Administration Punishments Law of the People's Republic of China; where a crime is constituted, criminal liability shall be investigated according to law.

Article 31 The administrative department for electric power under the State Council may, in accordance with these Regulations, formulate implementation measures.
The people's governments of provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government may, in accordance with these Regulations, formulate measures for the administration of small power grids.
Article 32 These Regulations shall be interpreted by the administrative department for electric power under the State Council.
Article 33 These Regulations shall come into force as of November 1, 1993.
